CLAIMS (ranked)

- claim: The method is prompt-only inference: the reasoning model (QwQ-32B-Preview) emits a search query between special tokens mid-reasoning, generation pauses, documents are fetched, a separate "Reason-in-Documents" pass by the same model condenses them, and only the condensed text is spliced back into the chain. No training.
  number: none
  setup: QwQ-32B-Preview, Bing Web Search API, top-k 10, Jina Reader for page bodies, max 32,768 tokens, temp 0.7
  quote: "the knowledge refinement module, which selectively integrates only relevant and concise information into the reasoning chain through a separate generation process using the original reasoning model." / "Once a new pair of special symbols for the search query is detected in the reasoning sequence, we pause the reasoning process, and the search query q(i)search is extracted."
  where: p.5 (Sec 3.3, 3.4)

- claim: Implementation settings.
  number: top-k 10; 32,768 max tokens; 8 A800-80GB
  setup: all retrieval methods
  quote: "we utilize the open-sourced QwQ-32B-Preview [54]. For generation settings, we use a maximum of 32,768 tokens, temperature of 0.7, top_p of 0.8, top_k of 20, and a repetition penalty of 1.05 across all models. For retrieval, we employ the Bing Web Search API, setting the region to US-EN and the top-k retrieved documents to 10. We use Jina Reader API to fetch the content of web pages for given URLs. For all retrieval-based methods, following [52], we apply a back-off strategy where, when a final answer is not provided, we use the result from direct reasoning." / "All experiments are conducted on eight NVIDIA A800-80GB GPUs."
  where: p.8 (Sec 4.3)

- claim: On GPQA diamond, Search-o1 beats direct reasoning, standard RAG and the agentic baseline without refinement (RAgent) — the ablation for Reason-in-Documents is Search-o1 vs RAgent-QwQ-32B.

LIMITS
- No training anywhere; results are prompt + inference scaffolding on one backbone (QwQ-32B-Preview). No other LRM tested.
- No cost, latency, token count, or number-of-search-calls figures are reported; batch inference (Algorithm 1, p.6) is described qualitatively only. Reason-in-Documents is an extra full generation per search step with the same 32B model.
- Depends on live Bing Web Search + Jina Reader; web results are non-reproducible and may contain benchmark answers (no contamination check on web content).
- Small reasoning test sets: GPQA diamond 198, AMC 40, AIME 30, LCB 112; single-run Pass@1 at temperature 0.7, no variance or seeds. QA test-set sizes are not stated.
- Reason-in-Documents ablation is only Search-o1 vs RAgent, but RAgent also differs in retrieval format (snippets + optional URL fetch vs full pages via Jina), so it is not a clean one-variable ablation.
- No gain on code (33.0 = direct), ties on AIME/AMC vs RAgent, small drop on 2Wiki (58.0 vs 58.4) and TriviaQA below standard RAG (63.4 vs 65.6/65.8); Llama3.3-70B direct beats all 32B methods on NQ/TriviaQA.
- Case study (p.21) shows the refinement module hallucinating a conclusion ("product 3 should have 10 carbon atoms") that the main chain later overrides — refinement can inject wrong reasoning, not just facts.
- Dated: QwQ-32B-Preview (Nov 2024), DeepSeek-R1-Lite and o1-preview as comparators; "Work in progress" v1.

BUILDS ON
- ReAct, Yao et al. 2022 [70] — RAgent baseline format (snippets then URL fetch).
- Agentic RAG precedents cited: MindSearch (Chen et al. 2024 [5]), PlanxRAG (Verma et al. 2024 [56]).
- Self-RAG, Asai et al. 2023 [1] — cited only as end-to-end trained RAG, not as a method basis.
- Self-Ask / IRCoT: NOT cited as methods. Press et al. 2023 [47] is cited only as the source of Bamboogle. IRCoT is not cited at all.
- Document compression/refinement lineage: RECOMP (Xu et al. 2023 [64]), LongLLMLingua (Jiang et al. 2023 [24]), BIDER (Jin et al. 2024 [27]).
- GPQA back-off strategy from Rein et al. 2023 [52]; CoT prompting from Wei et al. 2022 [59].

CODE
- Special tokens (p.5): `<|begin_search_query|> ... <|end_search_query|>` and `<|begin_search_result|> ... <|end_search_result|>`.
- Algorithm 1 core loop (p.6): "Generate all sequences in S until EOS or <|end_search_query|>" → "Retrieve documents: D ← Search(qsearch)" → "Construct input for Reason-in-documents: ID ← Idocs ⊕ qsearch ⊕ Seq" → batch "Reason-in-documents: Tr ← M(Ir)" → "Insert <|begin_search_result|>, rfinal, <|end_search_result|>".
- Reason-in-Documents prompt output contract (p.18): "If the web pages provide helpful information for current search query: Present the information beginning with ‘Final Information‘ ... If the web pages do not provide any helpful information ... Output ... Final Information / No helpful information found."
- Note (p.20): "we input them as user prompts, not system prompts."
- Code: https://github.com/sunnynexus/Search-o1

FIGURES
- Figure 2, p.4: three-panel comparison (vanilla reasoning / agentic RAG with raw docs / Search-o1 with Reason-in-Documents) on the trans-cinnamaldehyde carbon-count example. Best single picture of "why refine before inject"; shows wrong answers 14 and 10 vs correct 11.
- Figure 1, p.2: bar chart of hedge-word frequency ("perhaps", "alternatively", "wait", "likely") for direct / standard RAG / Search-o1 — concrete motivation for mid-reasoning retrieval.
- Figure 3, p.9: Pass@1 vs top-k (1,2,3,5,10) on GPQA with flat lines for direct reasoning and standard RAG k=10 — shows k=1 agentic beats k=10 standard.
- Algorithm 1, p.6: batched inference loop; useful for the "context discipline" section (refinement is a separate generation, not in the main chain).
- Table 6, p.23: HotpotQA trace with 5 searches and the search-limit refusal — good illustration of a step budget.

PROBLEMS
- The sentence "exceeds RAgent-QwQ-32B and QwQ-32B by 4.7% and 3.1%" (p.9) appears to have the two numbers swapped: recomputing from Table 1 five-dataset averages gives Search-o1 64.9 vs RAgent 63.0 (+3.0% relative) and vs QwQ 62.0 (+4.7% relative). All percentage gains in the paper are relative, not absolute points.
- MAX_SEARCH_LIMIT and MAX_URL_FETCH values are never printed; the limit of 5 is inferred from the Table 6 trace only.
- Open-domain QA test-set sizes are not stated.
- Figure 1 and Figure 3 numeric values exist only as plot labels; Figure 3 values are not recoverable from text.
- References [41]/[42] and [80]/[81] and [84]/[85] are duplicates.
- No embedded instructions found in the PDF text.
